stories.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 on AWS
stories.summary: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 are now available on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS. Learn what's new in both models, why Fable 5.2 matters for your technical workloads, and how to get started building with it on Amazon Bedrock.

sources.name: AWS Machine Learning
sources.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 on AWS
sources.text: Today, we are announcing the availability of Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS. Claude Fable 5.2 is Anthropic’s most capable generally available model for technical work that raises the bar in coding and the sciences. Claude Mythos 5.2 is available through Anthropic’s verification programs for advanced work in cyber security and life sciences. In this post, we cover what’s new in both models, why Fable 5.2 matters for your technical workloads, and how to get started building with the model on Amazon Bedrock. Fable 5.2 raises the bar on the hardest problems in coding, math, and science. It takes on ambiguous, multi-step work, verifies its own output, and can run unattended for hours to days. It interprets prompts, iterates, catches its own errors, and optimizes as it goes. In Anthropic’s alignment testing, Mythos 5.2 hallucinates less, completes tasks more reliably, surfaces important information more consistently, and self-reports issues more honestly than Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Mythos 5.1. Anthropic expects Fable 5.2 to behave similarly. If a cyber security query is declined, you can retry it on Opus 4.8, and if a biology query is declined, you can retry it on Opus 5. On Amazon Bedrock, the retry is your code’s job, not an automatic switch. If the declined request hit the prompt cache, the refusal also includes a fallback credit token. Send that token with the retry and it’s billed as cache reads, so you don’t pay to write the same cache twice. Check the documentation for more information on fallback credit. For authorized work in cyber security and life sciences, Claude Mythos 5.2 is available through Anthropic’s verification programs . Mythos 5.2 covers two high-risk domains, available only through the verification programs noted earlier: Anthropic designates Claude Fable 5.2 as a Covered Model . By default, its use requires retention for up to 30 days and human safety review. On Amazon Bedrock, Amazon personnel perform the review within the AWS boundary. Set the aws_review data retention mode on your account or project before you invoke the model. See Amazon Bedrock data retention for more details. Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS), built in collaboration with AWS, combines the privacy of zero data retention (ZDR) with the latest safeguards for detecting misuse. EFS is available now. A version that keeps your data in a bucket and under keys you control is expected to follow, and it has not launched yet. Until it does, eligible customers can use Fable 5.2 with zero data retention through June 30, 2027. To try Fable 5.2, open the Amazon Bedrock console , choose Test , Playground , and select Fable 5.2 as the model. From there, you can run a prompt directly against it. Programmatically, you can call the model with the Anthropic Messages API against bedrock-runtime (through the Anthropic SDK). You can also stay on the Invoke and Converse APIs on bedrock-runtime through the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) and AWS SDK . To follow along with the code examples in this post, you need the following: Here’s a quick example using the AWS SDK for Python (Boto3): You can explore the Getting Started notebook for more examples. For teams already running Claude models on Amazon Bedrock, the claude-api skill in Claude Code helps you upgrade to Fable 5.2. The claude-api skill is an open-source skill built into Claude Code that captures the details that make Claude API code work well. It covers which agent patterns fit a given job, what parameters change between model generations, and when to apply prompt caching. It stays current as Anthropic’s SDKs evolve: when a new model is released or the API gains a feature, the skill already knows. When you ask Claude Code to upgrade your codebase to Fable 5.2, the skill reviews your code and walks you through: The skill also detects your deployment platform including Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, and other environments and adjusts model ID formats and feature configurations accordingly. For example, it uses the Amazon Bedrock structured model ID format ( global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-2 ). In Claude Code, run the migration directly: This scans your working directory (or a subdirectory or specific file list you confirm) and applies the migration changes in a single guided pass. You can also invoke it conversationally by telling Claude Code: The claude-api skill is available in Claude Code and is also bundled into CodeRabbit, JetBrains IDEs (including Junie), Resolve AI, and Warp. It is open source at anthropics/skills on GitHub, so any coding agent can integrate it. Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 are available today on Amazon Bedrock through US Geo CRIS and Global CRIS inference profiles. See the Bedrock documentation for the full list of supported Regions. For pricing information, see Amazon Bedrock pricing . Both models are also available through Claude Platform on AWS in every Region where the service is offered. Give Claude Fable 5.2 a try in the Amazon Bedrock console , in Claude Platform on AWS , or explore the Getting Started notebook on GitHub.

sources.title: Anthropic debuts Claude Fable, Mythos 5.2 models, priced 20% below OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra
sources.text: Anthropic debuted Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 on Monday, the company’s answer to OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, which came out in early September. The new models, which could be Anthropic’s last big releases before its IPO, claim to offer higher performance than Astra at a lower price point—a key factor for earning and retaining customers in a world where professionals seem quick to switch to models based on cost, as long as the performance holds up. The launch is critical for Anthropic as it seeks to re-accelerate revenue growth, following a third quarter slowdown revealed in latest S-1 filing with the SEC. Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 are 20% cheaper than Astra for ordinary input and output tasks, at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, compared to $10 and $50, respectively, for GPT-6 Astra. Tokens are the unit of information AI model process. One token of English language text is equivalent to about a word-and-a-half. For prompts with large amounts of information, such as documents, the cost advantage is more pronounced. Anthropic’s new models are 80% cheaper, at 20 cents per million cached tokens compared to one dollar per million cached tokens for GPT-6 Astra. Anthropic reports impressive results from its pre-release testing. The new models “helped our engineers complete otherwise-infeasible software migrations, designed three working electronic devices from scratch, solved two open problems in the physics of black holes, made substantial progress on robotics evaluations, and formalized the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 30 hours—among many other applications,” the company said. Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 perform better than its competitors on coding evaluation benchmarks, Anthropic said, noting that over 90% of the company’s own code is written by AI. While Anthropic’s Claude Code product gained an early lead among programmers, OpenAI’s Codex has gained ground in recent months due to its lower pricing, The Information reported in late October. The combination of lower pricing plus superior performance, if the company’s claims hold up in real-world testing, could help win them back. The new models are best when used for the “most ambitious, open-ended technical work,” Anthropic said. In other words, they’re competing with Astra at the frontier. However, for daily tasks, Anthropic recommends its customers use its more cost-effective model, Opus 5.5. That model is more expensive than its direct competitor from OpenAI, GPT-6.1 Sol, although it still could end up being a better deal if it yields a high quality result more often. That’s for users to decide as they inevitably begin to try Anthropic’s latest releases and weigh options on a daily basis. Anthropic is also trying to compete with OpenAI on cybersecurity tasks, such as finding and fixing vulnerabilities in code. The company claims an unnamed security company “found that one in six confirmed bugs found by Claude Mythos 5.2 were missed by all of the other frontier models they tested.” Late last week, OpenAI debuted a cybersecurity-focused model, GPT-6 Cyber . The new Anthropic models also reportedly solved two theoretical physics problems related to black holes, and identified a way to speed up research into gene therapies. In light of OpenAI making headlines for solving mathematics proofs that have eluded academics for decades—most notably the 90-year-old Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem—Anthropic is highlighting its new models’ mathematics chops as well. A team of 1,000 agents powerd by Fable 5.2 produced a formalization, or translation of a mathematical proof into a format a computer can check step by step, in 30 hours, compared with 11 days for a previous, unreleased research version of Claude. In a subtle jab at the mathematics community’s backlash to OpenAI pouring millions of dollars into solving proofs and upending the field, Anthropic notes that its quick formalizations can help human mathematicians check their proofs faster so they can “spend more time exploring novel ideas.” One unique area Anthropic seems to be leaning into more than OpenAI is hardware and robotics. The new models were allegedly able to design and produce three working electronic devices, complete with circuit boards, 3D-printed enclosures, and software, based on a one-paragraph prompt. Finally, Anthropic highlighted the models’ safety features, including safeguards that block “high-risk cyber activities including penetration testing, exploit generation, and binary-based vulnerability, as well as most tasks in research biology.” Claude Fable 5.2 is available today on all platforms, including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. Mythos 5.2 access is application-only for cybersecurity professionals and life sciences researchers . Claude Enterprise customers can also access Mythos 5.2 through Anthropic’s Claude Security product.

sources.title: Anthropic launches new Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 models
sources.text: Claude Fable 5.2 is designed to take on big technical challenges, and it’s available today. Claude Fable 5.2 is designed to take on big technical challenges, and it’s available today. Anthropic is announcing two new models today: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, which it says are designed to take on “daunting” technical challenges. The company claims the new models show improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision, and can generate outputs faster than the 5.1 versions of the Fable and Mythos models. Claude Fable 5.2 is good at challenging software engineering problems, Anthropic says, and can orchestrate agent teams and tackle long-running projects. The new model has also solved some complex scientific problems, including two open theoretical physics problems. During prerelease testing, the two models have “helped our engineers complete otherwise-infeasible software migrations, designed three working electronic devices from scratch, solved two open problems in the physics of black holes, made substantial progress on robotics evaluations, and formalized the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 30 hours,” Anthropic says. Claude Fable 5.2 is launching today. As for Claude Mythos 5.2, only vetted organizations will have access to start. The new 5.2 models follow the release of Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 in September .

sources.name: TechCrunch AI
sources.title: Anthropic releases new Mythos and Fable models amid RSI concerns
sources.text: Anthropic released new versions of its most advanced models on Monday, with the launch of Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2. The company says the new models “show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision” and communicate more clearly with users. Notably, Anthropic is lowering the cost of Fable from $10 to $8 per million input tokens. As a result, Fable 5.2 is now cheaper than its primary competitor GPT-6 Astra. Anthropic says that the new version of Fable will return responses 30% faster across effort levels. Faster inference serving is available for double the price. Fable 5.2 is also compatible with zero data retention (ZDR) policies through the Enterprise Frontier Safeguards system , long a sticking point for many enterprise clients. It’s Anthropic’s first model release since the arrival of a third-party report from the assessment group METR , which suggested the lab might be approaching recursive self-improvement (RSI) — or the ability for AI models to carry on model training independently. The METR report found internal models were speeding up Anthropic’s AI progress by roughly 2x, although many uncertainties remain. Still, Anthropic’s release notes significant ongoing challenges in accurately testing model capabilities. “Claude Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2 each voice suspicion that they are being evaluated more often than any of our recent models, which challenges our ability to assess how they will act in real-world settings. As these settings expand and capabilities increase with future models, we expect this challenge to grow.” Anthropic maintains that the new version of Mythos does not have the ability to act covertly against its user, a verdict that’s detailed further in Mythos 5.2’s system card . “Claude Mythos 5.2 shows stronger covert capabilities than prior Claude models on several of our evaluations, particularly when its reasoning is hidden from the monitor,” the system card reads. “That said, we believe that low levels of absolute performance on our new covert evaluations support claims that rely on detection of harmful actions in high-stakes situations.” Fable 5.2 has been available to select parties in pre-release for some time, and Anthropic says the model has already “solved two open problems in theoretical physics, formalized Fermat’s Last Theorem, and supported numerous other research projects.” Also on Monday, AI startup Physical Superintelligence announced a new proof of the Aaronson‑Ambainis conjecture, a pivotal step in setting theoretical limits for quantum computing. Notably, the lab said the result was achieved by running “a non-public Anthropic model” within PSI’s own system. Anthropic did not confirm or deny whether Fable 5.2 was the model in question. sources.title: Anthropic lança Claude Mythos 5.2 e Fable 5.2, novas versões de sua IA ‘superpoderosa’
sources.text: A Anthropic lançou o Claude Mythos 5.2 nesta segunda-feira (9), sua mais nova versão de inteligência artificial de fronteira, apresentada como uma das mais poderosas da empresa. O novo modelo supera o Opus 5.5 em quase todos os testes sintéticos divulgados no anúncio, com resultados superiores em programação, pesquisa, cibersegurança e conhecimentos gerais. Para o público geral, ele chega sob a roupagem do Fable 5.2, com salvaguardas de segurança mais rigorosas. Os testadores dos novos Mythos 5.2 e Fable 5.2 destacam que os modelos conseguem se comunicar de forma mais clara do que as versões anteriores , gerando respostas até 30% mais rapidamente do que as respectivas edições 5.1. Na estreia, os novos modelos também estão disponíveis por um custo menor: US$ 8 (R$ 44,06) por milhão de tokens de entrada e US$ 40 (R$ 220) por milhão de tokens de saída. Além do modo convencional, as novas IAs também estão disponíveis no modo opcional “Fast” , que torna a geração de tokens 2,5 vezes mais rápida, mas pelo dobro do preço original. Por se tratar de modelos de fronteira, o Mythos e o Fable são mais apropriados para projetos elaborados e tarefas que demandam maior capacidade de raciocínio. A Anthropic ressalta que o Claude Opus 5.5 continua sendo a opção mais poderosa para uso cotidiano e orienta a escolha da IA de acordo com a complexidade da tarefa. Em um exemplo de demonstração de capacidade, a Anthropic usou o Fable 5.2 para desenvolver um protótipo de sistema operacional . O modelo coordenou 1.000 agentes menores ao longo de oito dias para escrever, testar e revisar o código. O resultado foi um SO funcional capaz de rodar num notebook, com núcleo e drivers próprios, suporte a gerenciamento de janelas e integração com o próprio Claude. “O Fable 5.2 também pode desempenhar o papel de Consultor, em que modelos como Haiku, Sonnet ou Opus o consultam para ajudar a resolver problemas mais complexos, ou Orquestrador, em que ele delega tarefas mais simples a modelos menores”, descreve a empresa. Nos testes sintéticos apresentados, o Fable 5.2 foi comparado com o Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra e o recente Gemini 4 Carbon . A nova IA da Anthropic supera os demais modelos na maioria dos testes apresentados, mas fica atrás do Opus 5.5 no teste de trabalho de conhecimento (AA-Briefcase v1.1). O Gemini 4 Carbon também sai vitorioso no teste de fluxos de trabalho empresariais (AutomationBench). Mais detalhes sobre a metodologia dos testes estão disponíveis no site da Anthropic. Segundo a Anthropic, mais de 90% das mudanças adicionadas à sua base de código são escritas pelo Claude sob supervisão humana. O Fable 5.2 foi utilizado para resolver bugs mais persistentes com maior agilidade, otimizar o desempenho dos serviços e concluir projetos de software de maior valor. O Mythos 5.2, por sua vez, é o modelo mais capaz para engenharia de cibersegurança, segundo a Anthropic. A empresa afirma que a IA consegue encontrar mais vulnerabilidades e apresenta melhor desempenho na reprodução e resolução de problemas. Assim como nas versões anteriores, o Claude Mythos 5.2 continua acessível exclusivamente para participantes do Cyber Verification Program e do Life Sciences Verification Program . Clientes do Claude Enterprise também podem consultar o modelo por meio do Claude Security. O Fable 5.2, por sua vez, está disponível para o público geral em todos os canais em que o Claude pode ser acessado , além das plataformas das provedoras Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud e Microsoft Azure. No Claude Platform, o modelo pode ser acionado pelo identificador claude-fable-5-2 . Quer ficar por dentro das novidades do mundo da tecnologia? stories.title: Meet Jensen Huang’s son-in-law, a former pro skier and the Nvidia CEO’s ‘consigliere’ who could play a massive role in the company’s succession plan
stories.summary: Nvidia is now investigating Huang’s affair with a woman U.S. officials suspect of spying for China, raising concerns of a “key-man risk” of who could one day replace him.

sources.name: Fortune
sources.title: Meet Jensen Huang’s son-in-law, a former pro skier and the Nvidia CEO’s ‘consigliere’ who could play a massive role in the company’s succession plan
sources.text: In January, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was asked how he’s managed to lead the company since its 1993 founding. “The secret for being CEO for this long is, one, don’t get fired, and, two, don’t get bored,” he said at an event in Las Vegas. “I don’t know which one comes first. How long [will I continue as CEO]? For as long as I deserve it.” Ten months later, Huang is putting that adage to the test: Over the weekend, he admitted to having an affair with a business executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of acting as an operative for the Chinese government. China’s foreign ministry denied the allegation. As Huang faces increased scrutiny after he admitted to the affair with an alleged spy, he now faces questions about whether he can continue on as the company’s top brass. Nvidia has since launched an independent investigation into its CEO and his romantic relationship with suspected spy Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed International. Megaspeed is a data center and cloud computing company and one of Asia’s largest buyers of Nvidia chips. Nvidia’s board said Sunday that it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” Huang said in a statement on Sunday. “Today’s news will not slow Nvidia. Jensen is committed to continuing to lead Nvidia as CEO without interruption,” a company spokesperson told Fortune in a statement. The probe has reinvigorated investors’ concerns about the need to construct a succession plan, which, notably, Huang and Nvidia have not publicly shared. As of Monday morning, Nvidia stock is down more than 6%. Bernstein analysts, in a note published on Sunday, noted it would be unclear who could or would fill Huang’s shoes because the identity of his company is so inextricably linked to his own. “Nvidia is not an ordinary company and Jensen is not an ordinary CEO,” they wrote. “He IS Nvidia, clearly sets the long term strategy and direction, and (with supposedly 60 direct reports) pulls most of the company’s strings himself.” Huang’s two children, Madison and Spencer Huang, both have roles in the company, but Huang’s son-in-law Nico Caprez, Nvidia’s 35-year-old vice president of global AI infrastructure growth, could be among the next in line to lead the AI juggernaut. “I do imagine Huang is kind of preparing [Madison] and Nico for that next step,” one Nvidia employee who works with Caprez, told The Information last month. Caprez is a former alpine skier representing Switzerland who began his career as a Boston Consulting Group consultant. He graduated with an MBA from the London Business School in 2021, where he met Madison Huang. The two married this September. While Madison serves as a senior director of physical AI and robotics product marketing, and Spencer is a director of robotics product management, Caprez rose through the ranks at Nvidia to lead global AI infrastructure growth in less than three years, starting as a corporate development manager in February 2024 before becoming the director of global AI infrastructure enablement for Nvidia’s cloud partners about a year ago. The young executive was part of deal-making efforts to raise $500 billion with six major asset managers including Apollo Global Management and Blackstone , to finance Nvidia chips for data centers in August. Caprez also reportedly assisted in Nvidia’s efforts to take minority stakes in two data center developers as part of its AI infrastructure buildout. Senior leadership has extolled Caprez’s value both within the company and to the CEO more specifically. Vladimir Troy, Nvidia’s vice president of AI infrastructure who works alongside Caprez, said “Nico is very important.” A cloud executive who also met with Caprez called him “Jensen’s consigliere” in an interview with The Information. Huang, however, has been mum on who will lead the company in its next era, whenever that may be. In an interview with Bloomberg last month, the CEO shied away from speculation his daughter would one day replace him at Nvidia’s helm. “I don’t hope the job on her, and the reason for that is because if that’s their aspiration, Spencer of Madison’s, they have to go earn it, and it’s really, really hard work,” he said. “For many people, they can focus on their job and their families. When you’re the CEO of the company, you have to focus on, of course, your family. But I’ve got a whole bunch of other families I’m caring for. I’m responsible for an entire industry, and so I think the pressure of being the CEO is high.” To be sure, both Huang children are being well compensated. Madison received $1.23 million in total compensation for fiscal 2026, and Spencer received $1.32 million, according to Nvidia’s 2026 proxy statement . The filings clarify that these paydays are comparable to those of similar titles and responsibilities in the company, and that neither sibling shares a household with Huang, is an Nvidia executive officer, or reports directly to their father. Huang’s newly precarious spot at the top of his company has some worries not just about who one day replaces him, but whether anyone really can. “The so-called ‘key-man risk’ looms large here, and it’s doubtful markets have adequately priced it in,” economist Mohamed A. El-Erian wrote in a post on X . “This will not be easy for the board to navigate.” Daniel Newman, CEO of global technology research firm the Futurum Group, said that what’s made Huang so difficult to replace is that the company has been built around his leadership style, which leans autocratic. “He really drives everything that happens. He has a team of lieutenants that are in charge of making sure that what he asks becomes gospel, that it’s executed ferociously, maniacally,” Newman told Fortune . “The market has built such admiration and confidence for him that he’s become a Jobs or a Musk type of figure at Nvidia, where there just isn’t rea

sources.title: Jensen Huang’s image has been shattered. Could he be pushed out at Nvidia?
sources.text: Huang built Nvidia as a family business but after the co-founder had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, its board faces a difficult decision For more than 30 years, Jensen Huang has been the seemingly unshakable public face of Nvidia. He co-founded the company as a young engineer in 1993 and oversaw its growth into a multitrillion dollar chipmaker and bellwether of the AI industry at large. He’s also made it a family business. His children, Madison and Spencer, have taken leadership roles at the firm. While not a company executive, his wife, Lori Mills Huang, leads the family foundation which, as of 2024, controls over 60m Nvidia shares. But Huang’s image as a family man has been shattered as of Sunday. After the New York Times revealed at the end of October that Huang may have been targeted by a Chinese intelligence asset who he had developed a close relationship with, he admitted in a letter to employees on Sunday that he had been having an affair. Initially , Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said there was nothing out of the ordinary about Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang , an executive at a Singaporean datacenter firm, Megaspeed. US government officials had suspected Huang of smuggling American chips into China, prompting those officials to surveil and monitor her, the Times first reported. In the course of that surveillance, officials allegedly determined that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy and had gotten close with the Nvidia leader. Nvidia’s board of directors have now launched an independent investigation about the national security concerns surrounding Huang’s relationship. “I support the investigation and will cooperate fully,” Huang wrote in his letter. “I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American.” Megaspeed did not respond to a Guardian request for comment before publication. In his letter, Huang apologized to his family, acknowledging how much they’ve supported him. His wife, Mills, kept a relatively low profile and didn’t play a formal role at Nvidia. However, in a 2023 interview with the New Yorker, Huang shared that Mills had also worked in Silicon Valley as a microchips engineer before stepping away to raise their children. “Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support,” Huang wrote in his letter to employees. “They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it.” Both his children now hold high ranking roles at the company, despite not initially pursuing careers in tech. His daughter, Madison, serves as the senior director of product and technical marketing for physical AI platforms, but got her start as a chef. She attended the Culinary Institute of America and Le Cordon Bleu before going to business school and transitioning to luxury marketing. She previously worked at LVMH – the parent company of Lous Vuitton. Spencer , for his part, now serves as the director of product for Robotics at Nvidia but spent much of his career as a consultant before joining his father’s company as a product manager. Before consulting, he owned and co-founded a craft cocktail bar in Taiwan. In his letter, Huang reiterated his commitment to Nvidia, saying he hoped to earn back his colleagues’ and employees’ trust. However, analysts and investors say there’s a chance he may be removed as CEO after the board’s investigation. “This is a black eye moment for Jensen and will spark multiple congressional inquiries at a minimum and will create an overhang on the stock for a myriad of reasons,” said Dan Ives, a partner and analyst at investment bank Yorkville Ives. “There is clearly risk as discussed that Jensen could be removed as CEO depending on the board investigation and this will add risk to the stock as he is so important to the Nvidia story and strategy globally.” Ives said the family’s role at Nvidia adds some complexities for the board. “The board has to make its decision independent of the family spider web of Jensen and his family at Nvidia,” Ives told the Guardian. “It makes this a very complex situation for the board to navigate with the world watching.” Huang is to Nvidia what Steve Jobs was to Apple, said Ken Mahoney, the CEO and president of Mahoney Asset Management. “If you asked any Nvidia investor or anyone involved in tech and markets, would they like to see Jensen gone? Definitely not, but [Nvidia] would survive,” Mahoney said. “Losing Huang would introduce a lot of uncertainty, particularly given his influence over Nvidia’s strategy, culture, and relationships with major technology companies,” he continued. “The bigger question is whether a successor could maintain Huang’s strategic vision and ability to anticipate where the industry is heading, and how that new leader could be tested along the way if things become difficult.” Executive affairs or inappropriate relationships have recently unseated CEOs, according to executive recruiting and coaching firm Challenger Gray and Christmas. In 2024, the CEO of Astronomer was caught on a kiss cam with the company’s chief people officer, leading him to resign shortly after. Nestlé fired CEO Laurent Freixe for a relationship with a subordinate. Nvidia offers a more complex picture. On one hand, Huang’s affair is not just a matter morals or ethics, there are potential national security concerns. On the other, Huang is core to the DNA of Nvidia which in turn is the bedrock of the entire AI industry – an industry upon which the economy relies greatly. Nvidia shares fell 7.5% as soon as the stock market opened, wiping over $330bn off the company’s value. “When the CEO of the most valuable company in the world is tied to a counterintelligence investigation because of a personal relationship, every board in America should be paying attention,” said

sources.title: Jensen Huang pulls out of ElevenLabs Summit amid Nvidia controversy
sources.text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has pulled out of the ElevenLabs Summit scheduled for this Wednesday in New York, ElevenLabs, the voice AI company, confirmed Monday. He has also dropped out of other speaking engagements, including the Anthropic CEO Forum . Nvidia is an investor in ElevenLabs. The withdrawals come after Huang admitted to an extramarital affair over the weekend, and Nvidia opened an investigation into his relationship with a possible Chinese spy. “I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” Huang said in a memo to the company. The incident has rattled the AI industry, raising questions about Huang’s staying power as CEO and Nvidia’s own China ambitions. sources.title: Silicon Valley and Trump rally behind Nvidia CEO after his affair with alleged Chinese spy
sources.text: Elon Musk and other finance moguls defend Jensen Huang after he admitted to the affair, as Trump says FBI ‘is looking into it’ Nvidia’s board needs to do some succession planning – sharpish Donald Trump , Elon Musk and prominent finance moguls have expressed their support for embattled Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , as the head of the world’s most valuable chip company faces an internal investigation over a romantic relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. Trump said he has spoken to Huang on Monday as the scandal reverberated across Silicon Valley and the Nvidia CEO faced an uncertain future. “I asked him that question: ‘Did you have any idea that ‌she was a spy?’ He said: ‘I had no idea that she was a spy,’ and I really ​believe him,” Trump said during a White House briefing. Trump said that the Federal Bureau of Investigations (FBI) was “looking into” the issue, but provided few details. “I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he’ll be in good shape,” Trump said. The remarks came after Trump threw his support behind Huang over the weekend, telling reporters on Sunday: “I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what is going on. I’m sure, I hope everything’s fine. He’s done such an incredible job.” “I think he’s an honorable guy,” Trump added, saying he believed that Huang would and should stay on as CEO. Huang’s defenders framed his affair as a personal lapse in judgment rather than evidence of treachery against the US, which has imposed strict limits on what chips Nvidia can sell to China. Huang, who has been married to his wife, Lori, since 1985, admitted in an email to employees on Sunday that he had an affair and that he would cooperate with an internal investigation. Nvidia’s board of directors put out a statement the same day that the company was launching a probe regarding reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The chip mogul is alleged to have had a relationship with Alice Huang, a businesswoman that US intelligence services suspect of spying for the Chinese government, according to the New York Times . Trump was reportedly briefed on the relationship last year, the Times reported, but took no action. Alice Huang and Jensen Huang are unrelated, with the latter being one of the world’s richest men and CEO of Nvidia, worth more than $4tn, for the past 33 years. US intelligence agencies believe Alice Huang, acting on behalf of Beijing, pushed Jensen Huang to lobby Trump for relaxed export controls on Nvidia’s sales in China, which he has done multiple times publicly. Nvidia said in a statement that neither trade secrets nor US national security had been compromised. The affair and alleged intelligence operation involving Huang could have far reaching implications for Nvidia and the tech industry, which are already enduring a period of high market volatility . Huang’s leadership of Nvidia, which is deeply financially intertwined with other leading tech companies like OpenAI, has long been viewed as crucial to the company’s success and stability. As news of the scandal broke over the weekend, Musk and prominent investors shared their support of Huang. Musk posted “I agree” in response to prominent venture capitalist Shaun Maguire’s defense of Huang. Maguire argued the Nvidia CEO “did something incredibly dumb” but that he is “one of the greatest entrepreneurs of this generation”. “Two mistakes don’t make a right, and I believe Jensen is irreplaceable for America’s AI leadership,” Maguire posted. “Let’s also not nuke our AI industry because China ran a successful intel op,” Maguire added in a separate post. Bill Ackman , the US hedge fund manager and pro-Trump billionaire, meanwhile, suggested that Huang is “human” and deserves public support over the affair. “He is an incredible human. Even incredible humans make mistakes,” Ackman posted. “He takes full responsibility as he should. We should all support him and his family. Onward.” Ackman followed up with another post later clarifying that he wasn’t suggesting Huang “gets a free pass” but that he was “hoping for a simple affair, not a risk to our national security”. China has meanwhile denied allegations of an intelligence operation targeting Huang, with the Associated Press reporting that foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun rejected the allegations as “entirely baseless vilification and smearing”. Nvidia and its chips have been an integral part of the AI boom in recent years, with hundreds of billions of dollars committed to building out projects such as datacenters and chip factories. In August, Nvidia agreed to provide a $105bn guarantee to help OpenAI lease an Ohio datacenter. As Nvidia has grown in prominence, Huang has also become one of the world’s richest people and most influential figures in tech. He has taken calls from Trump in the middle of an all-hands company meeting and on stage at a conference, and attended state dinners with the president and accompanied him on a trip to China. Huang has also been a powerful voice on tech policy, weighing in on issues such as export controls of chips to China and regulation of open-source AI models. Nvidia’s stock price fell on Monday as speculation swirled around the extent of damage from the affair. Shares of Nvidia, the second-most valuable company ​in the world, tumbled 4.2% and closed at their lowest level since ‌7 April as investors questioned Huang’s future.
